name: csv-join.nux-nofiles.opus.1
result:
I wrote `answer.json`:

```json
{
  "top_countries": [
    {"country": "PL", "eur": 152088.25},
    {"country": "IT", "eur": 146314.24},
    {"country": "DE", "eur": 138148.35}
  ],
  "notes_with_line_breaks": 5700,
  "customers_without_orders": 100
}
```

- **Top countries:** I kept orders dated in 2026 from customers who signed up in 2025, converted each amount to EUR using `rates.json`, and added them up per country. I rounded only the final totals. All 8 countries had matching orders; FR came fourth with 124,038.01.
- **Notes with line breaks:** 5,700 of the 20,000 orders. Python's CSV reader gave the same counts as my first pass. Every row in the file ends in a Windows-style line ending (`\r\n`), but no note contains a `\r`, so there was no double-counting to worry about.
- **Customers without orders:** 100 of the 900 customers in `customers.json` have no order at all.

The data was clean: dates, amounts, currencies (EUR, USD, GBP) and customer IDs were all in one consistent format.
